newsitem.title: CROATIA: New earthquake hits Croatian coast.
newsitem.headline: New earthquake hits Croatian coast.

text.p: An earthquake shook Croatia's Adriatic coast on Saturday, triggering landslides and causing fresh damage in the area hit by a series of quakes a few months ago, Croatian radio said.

The earthquake at 9.31 am (0731 GMT) measured 4.7 on the Richter scale and hit the same Ston-Slano area near the historic city of Dubrovnik which suffered a 6.0 quake in September 1996, the radio said.
It caused fresh damage to houses in the town of Ston and nearby villages, but no one was injured. The radio also reported minor landslides on the main coastal road.
Croatian television showed pictures of crumbling houses and said the quake destroyed the Bishop's Palace, an historic monument in Ston, one side of which collapsed onto the street.
The quake in September was followed by a series of aftershocks. Villagers were evacuated and some pitched tents near their damaged homes.
